steps.label: ELT
steps.sub: Load raw data first, THEN transform inside the target itself

eyebrow: The "T" in ELT — written entirely in T-SQL
code:
INSERT INTO dbo.FactInternetSales
  (ProductKey, OrderDateKey, SalesAmount, OrderQuantity)
SELECT dp.ProductKey, dd.DateKey,
  sod.UnitPrice * sod.OrderQty * (1 - sod.UnitPriceDiscount),
  sod.OrderQty
FROM Staging.SalesOrderDetail AS sod
JOIN dbo.DimProduct AS dp ON dp.ProductAlternateKey = sod.ProductID
JOIN dbo.DimDate AS dd ON dd.FullDateAlternateKey = CAST(sod.OrderDate AS DATE);
caption: Runs AFTER raw data is already loaded — this single statement IS the transform step.

eyebrow: Why ELT leans on T-SQL itself
code:
-- The transformation happens INSIDE the destination —
-- so an ordinary INSERT...SELECT with joins
-- IS the transformation engine
caption: Modern cloud warehouses lean ELT: destination compute is cheap, no separate transform tooling needed.
